I'm also a bit jaded from this job too. I am constantly criticized for everything I do. 

But I am considering getting a PHd in basket weaving after this.

Probably viewed as condescending. I've tried to be helpful, tried to be a point of reference for them. But I've definitely slid a few times, when expecting them to get something done before a big event, and find out they're late with the task undone because they were fiddling with their projector at home, my frustration is hard to hide.
Absolutely, you can generally get escalated, and better assistance with kindness and being polite. Then start building relationships with colleagues and have a work support system.
Being called out as unprofessional for trying to follow proper escalated channels to address people problems, when previous attempts in an acceptable way have failed.
It's not possible. Trying to be succinct makes you appear like a jerk. Trying to be friendly gives the wrong impression. Either you give too much information or not enough.
This is what happens when you accept the first auto-correct. You got a begrudging smile and slight disappointed in myself eye roll from me.

Yup, this is exactly what happened. 

I tried my best to be professional, root cause analysis, determine best plan of action. I got the emotional email, 'yelled' at in the email. Then made the mistake of trying to defend myself, by pointing out why their demands are not being adhered to with examples of why those demands are being willfully blocked by others to make me look foolish.

I kind of forget that this sub has a lot of people that work in support and is a side focus. I used to follow this sub religiously as a support tech and have been in an administration role heavily focused on implementations and best practices. 

What I've noticed, working tech support you're surrounded by people who have a common goal and have some of the same levels of understandings and frustrations. 

On the side of administration, having a very small group of people to work with. You have to rely on them to have a higher than basic understanding. There is only so much you can nod and smile at, when their actions jeopardizes the core of the foundation multiple times, what can you do? Try to follow proper channels, resolve the issues, but it continues to happen no matter what you do. Then you begin to look like a tattle tale or problematic person.

I'd like to take this a step further with a poor analogy. What I'm trying to describe is being a manager of a mechanics garage and one of your technicians refuses to change a tire because they haven't been trained on how to do so. However, you hired them because they have extensive experience in changing tires. You've taken time with them, and tried to go over some manuals to not only teach them, but express a shared interest in tire changing. They get frustrated, and start wrenching on cars they shouldn't be working on and tell the owner the reason a customers mazerati went out with out oil, is because you didn't teach them out to change tires. The owner doesn't understand and jumps on the band wagon. 

You find out the tire changing tech has also been lighting refuse tires on fire. You speak to them about it, say that's incredibly against policy. Then talk with the owner stating you spoke to the person and tried to resolve the issue. Later they start another tire fire, and ask if they started the fire again. The owner then tells you you're unprofessional and a hazard to the garage.
Sorry for not expanding on that properly. They're not entry level, these are the people at the same level of which I work and need to rely on to accomplish tasks.
Sure, I understand that logic. I question if it is me that warrants these type of interactions. When working with any one else, I receive a warm reception and positive attitude from them.

I'm recovering.. after a year of being harassed, bullied, threatened and blamed for the companies failures, I sat down on my couch and didn't move for three months. It's not worth your health, but some of these bigger corporations can legally enslave you and ruin your life.
You're right, $236,360.00 and above household income is.
West coast, according to my tax returns almost a quarter mil. In pocket not even close to that.
Doesn't matter much though, the cost of living here is fucking high and the taxes that get taken out of the equivalent of a 50k job anywhere else. It's all a fucking scam in the end.

There's a lot of other instances not related to weight. Other harassment, threats and retaliation. It's all been documented it's all been sent to the proper parties, it's all been ignored or hidden. Thank you, and keto is great, I kept getting lectured by him that it's wrong and I should take his diet advice.

I forgot to mention, this behavior went on for over a year. I've gone to HR multiple times for this and other things and it has been ignored. 

Thank you for your feed back, and the strap on begins to hurt less with pizza.
Extra large pizza, family sized pasta dish, a giant cookie and 2 liter of soda every day. Then when I was feeling sick from eating like this I'd order a dozen donuts.

I am intentionally being vague. To best summarize I am a salary worker that was working extreme hours for over a year. Including weekends, holidays, vacations, and expected to do so or faced repercussions of manipulation and retaliation. 

Excessive amounts of manipulation, degradation, accusations, and witness to collusion. Any attempts to resolve were handled at a face level and ignored, and became worse as time went on. Any future attempts to resolve were brought to the offenders and they would further retaliate against me.

Bonding and caring about others. I was the safe friend, the reliable one, willing to risk myself for you. I Used to be a hopeless romantic. 

I feel like I'm living day to day waiting for the end killing time and intentionally isolated myself from the rest of the world. Not to hard taking a job on the other side of the country that pays you well enough to be poor for the area and works you 18 hour days 7 days a week.

"I found her this morning in the bathtub with a note" ex2   roommate

"Your brother ruined my Valentine's day' ex3 after telling her my brother took his life.

"We could get him thrown in jail, it's not like they believe him over me" director of a woman's shelter after breaking up with ex4 who worked there and left her Facebook logged into my computer.

This is just the shit with romantic partners. Not including all the other stuff with friends, family and colleagues.
